CUTLASS issues found with Volta
===============================

Sources: CUTLASS at 5c179ede (main, 2026-11-25; external/ptx/sources/frameworks.txt), fetched
into target/ptx-sources/cutlass by external/ptx/extraction/fetch_sources.py. Each unit in
external/ptx/cutlass/units/ instantiates one kernel configuration, builds its launch with
CUTLASS's own host code and compiles for sm_100a (nvcc 12.9) by
external/ptx/extraction/cutlass.py. Verdicts are in external/ptx/output/cutlass.csv:

    uv run external/ptx/extraction/cutlass.py              # the 30 units
    uv run external/ptx/extraction/cutlass.py --patched    # the controls (FIXES), in patched/
    python3 external/ptx/races.py --framework cutlass

Volta treats floats as exact reals, so nothing below is a rounding difference. Every SM100
unit runs on one persistent CTA (sm_count 1) unless it says otherwise, so CTA 0 runs every
tile, the stage ring wraps and the TMEM accumulators are reused.

Part 1 is the issues Volta reports. Part 2 lists the units Volta cannot check yet, with what
stops each, and one open lead. Part 3 records the Volta changes the kernels needed.


1. Reported by Volta
--------------------

CL-1  SM100 (and SM90) TMA epilogues: every lane of the storing warp issues the same TMA store
      (benign race; redundant stores)
Where:    include/cutlass/epilogue/collective/sm100_epilogue_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:740 and
          :1100, `bool issue_tma_store = warp_idx == 0;` (comment: "one warp issues TMA
          store"); the same predicate in sm90_epilogue_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:714,
          sm100_epilogue_array_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:1175 and the two planar-complex SM100
          epilogues. Unchanged on CUTLASS main as of 2026-11-27.
Volta:    22 units RACE-CONDITION, memory-conflict freedom: WriteWrite on D's first bytes
          between two `cp.async.bulk.tensor.*.global.shared::cta.bulk_group` stores of the
          same subtile, issued by two lanes of epilogue warp 0 (threads 128-159):
          gemm_bf16_tn_128x128, gemm_bf16_nt_128x128, gemm_f16_nn_128x128,
          gemm_bf16_tn_colmajor_d, gemm_bf16_tn_64x128, gemm_f16_tn_128x256_f32,
          gemm_e4m3_tn_128x128_bf16, gemm_tf32_tn_128x128, gemm_bf16_tn_2stage,
          gemm_bf16_tn_batched, gemm_bf16_tn_clc, gemm_f16_tn_raster_m_swizzle2,
          gemm_bf16_tn_beta, gemm_bf16_tn_relu, gemm_bf16_tn_silu, gemm_bf16_tn_gelu,
          gemm_bf16_tn_row_bias_relu, gemm_bf16_tn_col_bias, gemm_e4m3_blockwise,
          gemm_mxfp8_blockscaled (also CL-2), gemm_bf16_tn_cpasync (also CL-3) and
          conv2d_fprop_f16 (the `.im2col_no_offs` store of the same epilogue).
What:     The store predicate selects the whole warp, and CuTe's SM90_TMA_STORE copy elects
          no lane (cute/arch/copy_sm90_tma.hpp: one `cp.async.bulk.tensor` per calling
          thread). So each of the warp's 32 lanes issues a TMA store of the same shared-memory
          subtile to the same global box, commits its own bulk group and waits for its own
          reads. The 32 stores write equal bytes, so the output is correct: a formal
          write-write race of equal values (Volta has no equal-store exception), and 32 TMA
          store operations per subtile where one suffices. In gemm_bf16_tn_128x128, D's
          128 x 128 tiles are stored as four 128 x 32 subtiles, each 32 times (op a43, a45,
          ... by t128, t129, ...). Whether the TMA unit merges the duplicates is undocumented;
          we have not measured it on hardware.
Fix:      elect one lane, as the array epilogue's other store path already does
          (sm100_epilogue_array_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:808, "a single thread from one warp
          issues TMA store"): `bool issue_tma_store = (warp_idx == 0) && cute::elect_one_sync();`
Status:   the fix (cutlass.py FIXES, built into patched/) makes every graph check pass on all
          22 units (with CL-2's and CL-3's fixes for those two); 18 are also proved equal to
          their specs (ACCEPT); gemm_bf16_tn_gelu, gemm_e4m3_blockwise and
          gemm_mxfp8_blockscaled have no spec (VERIFIED), and gemm_bf16_tn_silu's equivalence
          stays undecided. Reported upstream as NVIDIA/cutlass#3946 (2026-11-27).


CL-2  SM100 block-scaled GEMMs: the next k-tile's tcgen05.cp overwrites the Tensor Memory scale
      factors while the previous k-tile's MMAs may still read them (latent)
Where:    include/cutlass/gemm/collective/sm100_blockscaled_mma_warpspecialized.hpp:1018-1019 and
          :1065-1066, `copy(tiled_copy_s2t_SFA, thr_tCsSFA_s2t(_,_,_,_,read_stage),
          thr_tCtSFA_s2t)` (and SFB): one TMEM scale-factor buffer (`thr_tCtSFA_s2t` has no
          stage index), refilled every k-tile, then read by that k-tile's MMAs.
Volta:    gemm_mxfp8_blockscaled RACE-CONDITION, tensor-operation ordering: 12 WriteWrite
          conflicts between consecutive `tcgen05.cp.cta_group::1.32x128b.warpx4` of SFA (PTX
          line 1229) and of SFB (line 1234), and 768 ReadWrite conflicts between the four
          block-scaled `tcgen05.mma` of a k-tile (lines 1261, 1291, 1321, 1351) and the next
          k-tile's two copies, on the same Tensor Memory cells (column 256 on); nothing else.
What:     The MMA thread issues, per k-tile, tcgen05.cp of the stage's scale factors into the
          one TMEM buffer, then the MMAs that read them, then tcgen05.commit to free the
          shared-memory stage; the next k-tile's tcgen05.cp follows with no wait. PTX ISA 9.0
          9.7.16.6.2: "The asynchronous tcgen05 operations may execute and complete in a
          different order than they were issued", except five pipelined pairs, among them
          tcgen05.cp -> tcgen05.mma but neither tcgen05.mma -> tcgen05.cp nor tcgen05.cp ->
          tcgen05.cp. So nothing orders the copy after the earlier MMAs' scale reads: per the
          ISA an MMA may read the next k-tile's scales. It holds if the tensor pipe executes one
          thread's tcgen05 ops in order, which the ISA does not promise.
Reach:    every SM100 block-scaled CUTLASS GEMM through this collective (MXFP8, MXF4, NVFP4:
          examples 72a-c); the sm100 array, sparse, rcggemm and mixed TMA/cp.async block-scaled
          collectives and the sm103 and sm107 ones copy into an unstaged TMEM buffer the same
          way (read, not run).
Fix:      a tcgen05.fence::before_thread_sync before each refill (9.7.16.6.3: "An asynchronous
          tcgen05 operation prior to a tcgen05.fence::before_thread_sync is ordered before all
          subsequent tcgen05 and the execution ordering operations"), or double-buffering the
          TMEM scale factors by k-tile.
Status:   with the fence (cutlass.py FIXES) gemm_mxfp8_blockscaled's graph is VERIFIED (with
          CL-1's fix too). Reported upstream as NVIDIA/cutlass#3947 (2026-11-27; no earlier
          issue or PR: #3331 concerns which CTA issues the copy in 2-SM mode, #2974 is a fence
          question).


CL-3  SM100 cp.async GEMM mainloop: no proxy fence between the stage's cp.async writes (generic
      proxy) and the tcgen05.mma reads of them (async proxy) (latent)
Where:    include/cutlass/gemm/collective/sm100_mma_cpasync_warpspecialized.hpp: the producer
          (:510-520) copies a stage with cp.async and arrives with cpasync_barrier_arrive
          (`cp.async.mbarrier.arrive.shared::cta.b64`); the MMA warp (:565-577) waits on the
          stage and issues tcgen05.mma; neither runs fence.proxy.async (nor does the kernel,
          sm100_gemm_cpasync_warpspecialized.hpp). The mixed TMA/cp.async collectives
          (sm100_mma_mixed_tma_cpasync_warpspecialized.hpp and its block-scaled twin) have
          the same shape (read, not run).
Volta:    gemm_bf16_tn_cpasync (KernelWarpSpecialized1SmSm100, the CollectiveBuilder's non-TMA
          path) RACE-CONDITION, proxy ordering: ProxyOrderViolation WriteRead, missing
          ProxyAsync, between `cp.async.ca.shared.global` (PTX line 1762) and `tcgen05.mma`
          (line 2168) on a stage's bytes.
What:     PTX ISA 9.0 9.7.9.25.2: only "the cp{.reduce}.async.bulk operations are performed in
          the asynchronous proxy", so non-bulk cp.async writes shared memory through the generic
          proxy; 9.7.16.6.5: "The shared memory accesses by tcgen05.mma and tcgen05.cp operations
          are performed in the asynchronous proxy ... Accessing the same memory location across
          multiple proxies needs a cross-proxy fence ... fence.proxy.async". The mbarrier
          completion orders the copies before the MMA warp's wait, but no proxy fence makes them
          visible to the async proxy, so an MMA may read a stage's stale bytes.
Fix:      `cutlass::arch::fence_view_async_shared();` in the MMA warp after each consumer_wait.
Status:   with it (cutlass.py FIXES) gemm_bf16_tn_cpasync is RACE-FREE and ACCEPT (with CL-1's
          fix too). Already proposed upstream: NVIDIA/cutlass PR #3799 (open, 2026-10-29) adds the
          same fence to this collective and both mixed ones, after #3724's SM90 fix (#3721);
          reported as NVIDIA/cutlass#3948 (2026-11-27), citing it.


2. Units Volta cannot check yet, and open leads
-----------------------------------------------

V-1   gemm_bf16_tn_streamk: UNSUPPORTED, `ld.global.acquire.gpu.b32` (stream-K's cross-CTA flags;
      acquire/release atomic protocols are not modeled, and one CTA is analyzed).
V-2   fmha_fwd_f16_d128: the run aborts at a branch on a symbolic predicate (the online softmax's
      conditional rescale), so its graph is a prefix. On that prefix two further Volta gaps
      show: a tcgen05.ld is ordered before a later tcgen05.st of the same cells only by the
      register dependency (the S row maximum feeds the stored P statistics), which Volta does not
      model, and the allocating MMA warp's tcgen05.alloc reaches the softmax warps' TMEM uses only
      through the MMA's completion, which carries no thread's events in G_HB.

L-1   (open lead) gemm_bf16_tn_nosmem: with an empty epilogue storage the kernel's SharedStorage
      places smem_A 512 bytes past a 1024-byte boundary (TensorStorage is aligned_struct<128>,
      after the pipelines), 128B-swizzled, and CuTe's make_umma_desc always sets base_offset = 0
      (cute/arch/mma_sm100_desc.hpp:783). PTX ISA 9.0 9.7.16.4.1: "the base offset must be a
      non-zero value ... (pattern start addr >> 0x7) & 0x7" when the repeating pattern does not
      start at the 1024-byte boundary. Whether that applies depends on where a TMA-written tile's
      pattern starts (5.5.7 gives the TMA a swizzle base offset (dstMem / 128) % 8, i.e. absolute
      address bits) and on the dynamic shared memory base's alignment on hardware. Volta swizzles
      both TMA and MMA by absolute address bits, under which the kernel is ACCEPT.

Every other unit runs to a verdict: sm80_bf16_tensorop_relu, sm80_f16_tensorop,
sm80_f16_batched, sm80_sgemm_simt, sm80_tf32_tensorop and gemm_bf16_tn_nosmem are RACE-FREE and
ACCEPT; the rest are CL-1 and CL-2.


3. Volta changes the SM100 kernels needed
-----------------------------------------

Before these, every SM100 unit was UNSUPPORTED or CHECK-FAILED on Volta's own account:

- `clusterlaunchcontrol.try_cancel.multicast::cluster::all` (CUTLASS's default, stream-K and
  grouped schedulers) lowers as the plain request: every cluster holds one CTA.
- A warp collective other than `bar.warp.sync` (`elect.sync`, `shfl.sync`, ...) orders its
  lanes' execution in G0, not memory: the MMA warp's 32 lanes all wait on a stage, then
  elect.sync picks the lane that commits.
- An async completion joined into an mbarrier phase is admitted to G0 (each query reads only
  earlier joins, so a pass validates them by induction over the trace): the producer warp's
  non-leader lanes reach the next empty phase only through the TMA's completion of full.
- In G_HB an async op's completion carries the async effects that reached its issue (never
  the issuer's own accesses): a stage refill follows the stage's previous TMA load through
  TMA -> MMA -> tcgen05.commit -> refill. This settles open question (a) of
  volta_findings.txt for async-proxy chains.

The units Volta could not run at first needed, each with a test:

- Spaceless `ld`/`st` resolve each address through the generic windows (shared, param and a new
  local one); `cvta.global` and `cvta{.to}.local` are modeled (the SM80 GEMMs, cp.async, FMHA).
- A 32-bit word whose low half is zero, read by a float operation, is its high half widened to
  f32: nvcc's bf16-to-f32 (`shl.b32 16`, `and.b32 0xffff0000`), taking the halves as bf16 (the C
  and bias epilogues).
- `ld` takes its state space before the semantics (`ld.global.acquire.gpu`), as ptxas does.
- `call vprintf` is a no-op returning 0 (FMHA).
- `tcgen05.mma.kind::tf32`, K = 8 of 4-byte operands.
- A TMA box off its swizzle pattern's boundary is legal, with the base offset ISA 5.5.7 gives.
- A Tensor Memory address's top two bits select the cell's byte (CuTe's scale-factor IDs).
- The `.im2col_no_offs` TMA store (the conv epilogue).
- Two async tcgen05 operations of one thread with its tcgen05.fence::before_thread_sync between
  their issues are ordered (PTX ISA 9.7.16.6.3), a pipeline rule beside the ISA's pipelined pairs
  (CL-2's control).
